subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 2(47) of the CGST Act, 'exempt supply' means supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be wholly exempt from tax, and:

options.A: Includes non-taxable supply
options.B: Excludes non-taxable supply, which is treated as a separate category under GST
options.C: Is limited only to supplies which are conditionally exempt by way of a notification
options.D: Applies only to supplies of goods and does not extend to supplies of services

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. Includes non-taxable supply

As per section 2(47) of the CGST Act, exempt supply means supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be wholly exempt from tax and includes non-taxable supply. Thus, under GST, a supply not leviable to tax is also included within the purview of 'exempt supply'.

question_html: As per section 11(1) of the CGST Act, where the Government is satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest so to do, it may, on the recommendations of the Council, exempt goods or services or both from the whole or any part of the tax leviable thereon, by way of:

question_html: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes an absolute (unconditional) exemption from a conditional exemption under GST?

options.A: An absolute/unconditional exemption is mandatory in nature, and the registered person does not have the option to collect and pay tax on such supply; a conditional exemption is optional, and it is at the option of the registered person whether to avail it or not
options.B: Both absolute and conditional exemptions are mandatory in nature, and neither permits the registered person any option regarding collection of tax
options.C: An absolute exemption is optional in nature, while a conditional exemption is mandatory in nature, contrary to their common usage
options.D: Absolute exemptions apply only to goods, while conditional exemptions apply only to services, with no overlap between the two categories

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. An absolute/unconditional exemption is mandatory in nature, and the registered person does not have the option to collect and pay tax on such supply; a conditional exemption is optional, and it is at the option of the registered person whether to avail it or not

As explained in the Study Material, where the supply of goods or services is unconditionally exempted from whole or part of the tax, such exemption is mandatory and the registered person does not have the option to collect and pay tax. However, where the exemption is conditional, it is at the option of the registered person whether to avail the same or not.

question_html: As per section 11(3) of the CGST Act, where the Government inserts an explanation in a notification or order for the purpose of clarifying its scope or applicability, within one year of issue of the notification/order, such explanation shall have effect:

options.B: As if it had always been part of the first such notification or order, i.e. the explanation is effective retrospectively from the inception of the entry to which it relates, and not from the date the explanation-inserting notification itself becomes effective
options.A: Only prospectively, from the date on which the notification inserting the explanation is issued, and not before
options.C: Only for a period of one year from the date of insertion of the explanation, after which it ceases to have effect
options.D: Only if separately ratified by Parliament through an amendment to the CGST Act itself

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. As if it had always been part of the first such notification or order, i.e. the explanation is effective retrospectively from the inception of the entry to which it relates, and not from the date the explanation-inserting notification itself becomes effective

As per section 11(3) of the CGST Act, an explanation inserted within one year of issue of a notification/order shall have effect as if it had always been part of the first such notification/order. As clarified vide Circular No. 120/39/2019 GST dated 11.10.2019, such an explanation is effective from the inception of the entry in the notification, and not from the date on which the notification inserting the explanation itself becomes effective.

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 11A of the CGST Act, where the Government is satisfied that a practice was generally prevalent regarding non-levy (or short-levy) of central tax on any supply, and such supplies were actually liable to tax (or a higher amount of tax), the Government may, on the recommendation of the Council, direct that:

options.C: The whole of the central tax payable on such supplies, or the central tax in excess of that payable, but for the said practice, shall not be required to be paid, in respect of supplies on which tax was not, or is not being, levied, or was short-levied, in accordance with the said practice
options.A: Such supplies shall be retrospectively taxed at the highest applicable GST rate, irrespective of the general practice previously followed
options.B: The taxpayers who followed the general practice shall be liable to pay the differential tax along with interest and penalty, without any relief
options.D: The GST Council alone may grant such relief without any notification being issued by the Government in the Official Gazette

answer_html:
Correct Answer: C. The whole of the central tax payable on such supplies, or the central tax in excess of that payable, but for the said practice, shall not be required to be paid, in respect of supplies on which tax was not, or is not being, levied, or was short-levied, in accordance with the said practice

As per section 11A of the CGST Act (with an identical provision under section 6A of the IGST Act), where a generally prevalent practice existed regarding non-levy or short-levy of tax and the supplies were actually liable to tax or a higher rate, the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that the tax not levied or short-levied in accordance with such practice shall not be required to be paid, providing relief to taxpayers who followed industry practice in good faith.

question_html: As per Entry 1 of the Exemption Notification (services by an entity registered under section 12AA or 12AB of the Income-tax Act, 1961 by way of charitable activities), which two conditions must be cumulatively satisfied for a charitable trust's services to qualify for this exemption?

options.A: The entity must be registered under section 12AA or 12AB of the Income-tax Act, 1961, AND the entity must carry out one or more of the specified 'charitable activities' as defined in the Exemption Notification
options.B: The entity must be registered under section 12AA or 12AB of the Income-tax Act, 1961, OR the entity must have an annual turnover below the GST registration threshold (either condition being sufficient)
options.C: The entity must be a religious trust only, and charitable trusts not connected with religion are excluded from this exemption entirely
options.D: The entity must obtain a separate GST registration exclusively for its charitable activities, distinct from any other registration it may hold

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. The entity must be registered under section 12AA or 12AB of the Income-tax Act, 1961, AND the entity must carry out one or more of the specified 'charitable activities' as defined in the Exemption Notification

As per Entry 1 of the Exemption Notification, in order to claim exemption, two conditions must be cumulatively satisfied: (i) the entity should be registered under section 12AA or 12AB of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and (ii) the entity must carry out one or more of the specified charitable activities. Services falling outside the definition of 'charitable activities' remain taxable even if provided by such a registered entity.

options.A: Care or counselling of persons afflicted with HIV or AIDS, as part of public health activities

question_html: As per Entry 13(b) of the Exemption Notification, renting of precincts of a religious place meant for general public is exempt from GST EXCEPT where the charges for renting of rooms are:

options.D: Rs. 1,000 or more per day
options.A: Rs. 5,000 or more per day, irrespective of the type of space being rented

options.C: Rs. 10,000 or more per month, applicable uniformly to all categories of renting

answer_html:

question_html: As per the analysis of Entry 54 of the Exemption Notification, 'agricultural produce' means any produce out of cultivation of plants and rearing of all life forms of animals (except rearing of horses), on which:

options.D: Either no further processing is done, or such processing is done as is usually done by a cultivator or producer which does not alter its essential characteristics but makes it marketable for the primary market
options.A: Any degree of processing has been carried out, regardless of whether such processing alters the essential characteristics of the produce
options.B: Processing has been carried out exclusively by a registered manufacturer using industrial machinery at a factory premises
options.C: No processing whatsoever has been carried out at any stage, from harvesting through to final retail sale to the consumer

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. Either no further processing is done, or such processing is done as is usually done by a cultivator or producer which does not alter its essential characteristics but makes it marketable for the primary market

As explained in the analysis of Entry 54, 'agricultural produce' means any produce out of cultivation of plants/rearing of animals (except horses) on which either no further processing is done, or such processing is done as is usually done by a cultivator/producer which does not alter its essential characteristics but makes it only marketable for the primary market (not the retail market). Processing that alters essential characteristics (e.g. potato chips) or makes produce marketable in the retail market falls outside this entry.

question_html: Which of the following, as clarified in the Study Material (based on relevant CBIC circulars), is correctly classified as falling OUTSIDE the definition of 'agricultural produce' under Entry 54?

options.A: Processed tea (such as black tea, green tea), processed coffee beans/powder, dehusked or split pulses (dal), and jaggery obtained from processing sugarcane
options.B: Green tea leaves prior to any processing at a tea factory, which remain within the definition of agricultural produce
options.C: Whole pulse grains such as whole gram or rajma, which have not undergone dehusking or splitting
options.D: Raw sugarcane prior to any processing into jaggery, which remains within the definition of agricultural produce

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. Processed tea (such as black tea, green tea), processed coffee beans/powder, dehusked or split pulses (dal), and jaggery obtained from processing sugarcane

As clarified vide Circular No. 16/16/2017 GST dated 15.11.2017, processed tea (black/green/white tea), processed coffee beans/powder, dehusked or split pulses, jaggery, processed spices, processed dry fruits and processed cashew nuts fall outside the definition of 'agricultural produce' since these processes alter the essential characteristics of the produce or are not usually carried out by farmers/at farm level. Green tea leaves (unprocessed) and whole, undehusked pulse grains remain within the definition.

question_html: As clarified vide Circular No. 19/19/2017 GST dated 20.11.2017, is custom milling of paddy into rice eligible for exemption under Entry 55 of the Exemption Notification (intermediate production process as job work in relation to cultivation of plants)?

options.B: No, milling of paddy into rice is not eligible for exemption under Entry 55, since it is a process carried out after cultivation is complete, is not usually carried out by cultivators (but by rice millers), and changes the essential characteristics of the paddy
options.A: Yes, milling of paddy into rice is always exempt under Entry 55 as an intermediate production process in relation to cultivation of plants
options.C: Yes, but only when the milling is carried out by the farmer himself at his own agricultural farm using his own machinery
options.D: No, milling of paddy into rice is taxable under Entry 24 (loading, unloading, packing, storage or warehousing of rice) rather than Entry 55

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. No, milling of paddy into rice is not eligible for exemption under Entry 55, since it is a process carried out after cultivation is complete, is not usually carried out by cultivators (but by rice millers), and changes the essential characteristics of the paddy

As clarified vide Circular No. 19/19/2017 GST dated 20.11.2017, milling of paddy into rice is not an intermediate production process in relation to cultivation of plants - it is carried out after harvesting is complete, is usually done by rice millers rather than cultivators, and changes the essential characteristics of the produce. Therefore, it is not eligible for exemption under Entry 55.

question_html: As clarified vide Circular No. 32/06/2018 GST dated 12.02.2018, what is the GST treatment of food supplied by a hospital's canteen to (i) in-patients as advised by the doctor/nutritionist, and (ii) other patients (not admitted) or their attendants/visitors?

options.B: Food supplied to in-patients as advised by the doctor/nutritionist is part of the composite supply of health care and is not separately taxable (i.e. exempt); other supplies of food by the hospital to patients not admitted, or to attendants/visitors, are taxable

As clarified vide Circular No. 32/06/2018 GST dated 12.02.2018, food supplied to in-patients as advised by the doctor/nutritionist is a part of the composite supply of health care and is not separately taxable (exempt). question_html: As per Entry 62 of the Exemption Notification, services provided by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority by way of tolerating non-performance of a contract, for which consideration in the form of fines or liquidated damages is payable TO the Government under such contract, are:

options.A: Exempt from GST

question_html: Which of the following bodies is correctly included within the definition of 'local authority' under section 2(69) of the CGST Act?

options.B: A Panchayat as defined in Article 243 of the Constitution, a Municipality as defined in Article 243P, and a Cantonment Board as defined under the Cantonments Act, 2006
options.A: A local developmental authority set up by a State Government to undertake developmental works, such as the Delhi Development Authority or Bangalore Development Authority
options.C: A regulatory body/agency such as the Securities and Exchange Board of India or the Competition Commission of India
options.D: Any body merely described as a 'local body' by virtue of a local law, even if not specifically listed in the definition under section 2(69)

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. A Panchayat as defined in Article 243 of the Constitution, a Municipality as defined in Article 243P, and a Cantonment Board as defined under the Cantonments Act, 2006

As per section 2(69) of the CGST Act, 'local authority' includes only those bodies specifically listed: a Panchayat (Article 243), a Municipality (Article 243P), a Municipal Committee/Zilla Parishad/District Board (or other authority entrusted with control of a municipal/local fund), a Cantonment Board, a Regional/District Council under the Sixth Schedule, and Development/Regional Councils under Articles 371/371A/371J. Local developmental authorities like DDA or BDA, and regulatory bodies/agencies, are NOT covered by this definition.

question_html: As per Entries 10 and 11 of the Exemption Notification, services by way of PURE LABOUR CONTRACTS of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works are exempt in which of the following situations?

options.D: (i) Pertaining to beneficiary-led individual house construction/enhancement under the Housing for All (Urban) Mission/Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Entry 10); and (ii) pertaining to a single residential unit otherwise than as a part of a residential complex (Entry 11)
options.A: Pertaining to any residential complex comprising more than one single residential unit, regardless of whether the contract is a pure labour contract or a works contract involving materials
options.B: Pertaining to commercial construction projects undertaken by private developers, regardless of the nature of the contract or the beneficiary involved
options.C: Pertaining to any construction activity undertaken by the Central or State Public Works Department, regardless of whether it is a pure labour contract

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. (i) Pertaining to beneficiary-led individual house construction/enhancement under the Housing for All (Urban) Mission/Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Entry 10); and (ii) pertaining to a single residential unit otherwise than as a part of a residential complex (Entry 11)

As per Entry 10, pure labour contracts of construction/erection/commissioning/installation/completion/fitting out/repair/maintenance/renovation/alteration of a civil structure or original works pertaining to beneficiary-led individual house construction/enhancement under PMAY are exempt. As per Entry 11, pure labour contracts of construction/erection/commissioning/installation of original works pertaining to a SINGLE RESIDENTIAL UNIT (a self-contained unit designed for one family) otherwise than as part of a residential complex are exempt. question_html: As per the definition of 'goods transport agency' (GTA), the issuance of a consignment note is the sine qua non for a service provider to be considered a GTA. Which of the following statements correctly follows from this?

question_html: As clarified vide Circular No. 102/21/2019-GST dated 28.06.2019, where a seller (X) sells goods to a buyer (Y) and separately extends a loan to Y for payment in instalments (charging interest and additional/penal interest on delayed EMI payments, invoiced separately as a loan transaction), how is the additional/penal interest on the delayed instalment payment treated?

options.B: The additional/penal interest satisfies the definition of 'interest' under Entry 27 (being consideration for extending a loan/credit facility) and is therefore covered by the exemption; it is NOT treated as consideration for liquidated damages/tolerating an act under Schedule II
options.A: The additional/penal interest is always treated as consideration for liquidated damages under Schedule II ('agreeing to tolerate an act'), and is therefore a separate taxable supply of service in every case
options.C: The additional/penal interest is included in the value of the goods sold under section 15(2)(d) in every case, regardless of whether it is invoiced separately as part of a distinct loan transaction
options.D: The additional/penal interest is exempt only if the rate of penal interest does not exceed the rate of interest charged on the principal loan amount

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. The additional/penal interest satisfies the definition of 'interest' under Entry 27 (being consideration for extending a loan/credit facility) and is therefore covered by the exemption; it is NOT treated as consideration for liquidated damages/tolerating an act under Schedule II

As clarified vide Circular No. 102/21/2019-GST dated 28.06.2019, where the loan transaction is between the buyer (Y) and a genuinely distinct financing arrangement (e.g. a separate loan from a financier), and the additional/penal interest satisfies the definition of 'interest' under Entry 27, such penal interest is exempt and is NOT treated as consideration for liquidated damages under Schedule II. (Contrast this with a case where the seller itself invoices penal interest as part of the same sale transaction - there, per section 15(2)(d), the penal interest is included in the value of the goods supplied and is taxable.)

question_html: As per Entry 41 of the Exemption Notification, upfront amount (premium/salami/cost/price/development charges) payable in respect of a long-term lease (30 years or more) of industrial plots or plots for infrastructure development, provided by specified State entities to industrial units/developers, is exempt from GST. options.D: Also exempt, since allowing choice of location of the plot is an integral part of the supply of the long-term lease, and PLC charged upfront along with the lease premium is nothing but part of the consideration for the long-term lease

question_html: As per Entry 45 of the Exemption Notification, legal services provided by a partnership firm of advocates or an individual advocate (other than a senior advocate) are exempt when provided to which of the following recipients?

options.A: (i) An advocate or partnership firm of advocates providing legal services; (ii) any person other than a business entity; (iii) a business entity with aggregate turnover up to the GST registration exemption threshold; and (iv) the Central/State Government/UT/local authority/Governmental Authority/Government Entity

options.C: Only individuals who are themselves registered under GST as professionals, with unregistered individuals being excluded from the scope of this exemption
options.D: Only Government entities, with legal services to any person other than Government (including other advocates or small business entities) being fully taxable

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. (i) An advocate or partnership firm of advocates providing legal services; (ii) any person other than a business entity; (iii) a business entity with aggregate turnover up to the GST registration exemption threshold; and (iv) the Central/State Government/UT/local authority/Governmental Authority/Government Entity

question_html: Pyarelal & Co. obtained GST registration in the preceding financial year as its aggregate turnover exceeded the threshold exemption limit. question_html: As per Entry 2 of the Exemption Notification, services by way of transfer of a going concern, as a whole or an independent part thereof, are exempt from GST. Such a transfer (commonly referred to as a 'slump sale' when for a lump sum consideration):

options.A: Comprises a comprehensive sale of immovable property, goods and transfer of unexecuted orders, employees, goodwill, etc., of a running business capable of being carried on by the purchaser as an independent business - since the transfer is not merely a transfer of title to goods or immovable property, it may amount to a service and has thus been exempted

answer_html:

As per Entry 2, services by way of transfer of a going concern (as a whole or an independent part) are exempt. question_html: As per Entry 12 of the Exemption Notification, renting of a residential dwelling for use as residence is exempt EXCEPT where the residential dwelling is rented to a registered person. options.A: Where the registered person is a private limited company renting the dwelling for use as an employee's residence, since companies are treated identically to individual proprietors under this entry

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. Where the registered person is the proprietor of a proprietorship concern and rents the residential dwelling in his personal capacity for use as his own residence, and such renting is on his own account and not that of the proprietorship concern

As per Explanation 1 to Entry 12, the exemption for renting of residential dwelling for use as residence STILL covers renting to a registered person where: (i) the registered person is the proprietor of a proprietorship concern and rents the dwelling in his PERSONAL capacity for his own residence; and (ii) such renting is on his own account and not that of the proprietorship concern. In all other cases of renting to a registered person (e.g. a company renting for an employee's residential use), the exemption does not apply and GST is payable by the registered recipient under reverse charge.

question_html: Does Vidyodaya Public School qualify as an 'educational institution' under the Exemption Notification, and are its services to students exempt from GST?

options.B: No, since only institutions offering a curriculum leading to a law-recognised qualification (such as a university degree) qualify as educational institutions, and school-level education is excluded
options.C: Yes, but its services are exempt only if it does not charge any tuition fee whatsoever from its students, which contradicts the basic premise of a functioning school
options.D: No, since affiliation to a State education board (rather than a Central board like CBSE) disqualifies an institution from being treated as an educational institution

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. Yes, Vidyodaya Public School qualifies as an educational institution since it provides pre-school education and education up to higher secondary school, which is explicitly covered under sub-clause (i) of the definition; its services to students, faculty and staff are exempt under Entry 66(a)

As per sub-clause (i) of the definition of 'educational institution', an institution providing pre-school education and education up to higher secondary school or equivalent qualifies as an educational institution. case_facts_html: Case Scenario: Ananda Multispeciality Hospital, a clinical establishment, provides the following services in a month: (i) it admits a road accident victim requiring reconstructive plastic surgery to restore facial anatomy damaged in the accident; (ii) it charges an in-patient Rs. 4,500 per day for a private room (not an ICU/CCU/ICCU/NICU) during a 5-day hospital stay; and (iii) it separately charges another in-patient Rs. 6,200 per day for a deluxe private room (also not an ICU/CCU/ICCU/NICU) during a 3-day hospital stay.
question_html: Is the reconstructive plastic surgery performed on the road accident victim, to restore facial anatomy damaged in the accident, exempt from GST?

options.D: Yes, since the surgery is undertaken to restore or reconstruct anatomy or functions of the body affected due to injury or trauma (the road accident), it falls within the exception to the general exclusion of cosmetic/plastic surgery from 'health care services', and is therefore exempt
options.A: No, plastic surgery is categorically excluded from the definition of health care services in all circumstances, regardless of the underlying medical necessity
options.B: Yes, but only if performed free of any consideration whatsoever; any fee charged for reconstructive surgery renders the service taxable
options.C: No, since only surgeries relating to congenital defects (present from birth) qualify for this exception, and injuries sustained in accidents after birth are excluded

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. Yes, since the surgery is undertaken to restore or reconstruct anatomy or functions of the body affected due to injury or trauma (the road accident), it falls within the exception to the general exclusion of cosmetic/plastic surgery from 'health care services', and is therefore exempt

As per the definition of 'health care services', hair transplant or cosmetic/plastic surgery is generally excluded, EXCEPT when undertaken to restore or reconstruct anatomy or functions of the body affected due to congenital defects, developmental abnormalities, INJURY or TRAUMA. Since this surgery is reconstructive, addressing facial damage caused by an accident (trauma/injury), it falls within the exception and is exempt from GST under Entry 74(a).

subject: Goods and Services Tax
case_facts_html: Case Scenario: Vasundhara, a classical Odissi dancer, performs at three separate events in a financial year, each an independent, separately contracted engagement: (i) a solo classical Odissi performance at a State-level cultural festival, for a fee of Rs. 1,42,000; (ii) a classical Odissi performance specifically choreographed to promote a jewellery brand's new collection, as part of her engagement as the brand's ambassador, for a fee of Rs. 95,000; and (iii) a classical Odissi performance at a private wedding reception, for a fee of Rs. 1,65,000. Separately, at event (i), the festival organiser charges the audience an admission fee of Rs. 480 per person.
question_html: Is Vasundhara's fee of Rs. 1,65,000 for the performance at the private wedding reception taxable, and is the admission fee of Rs. 480 per person charged by the festival organiser at event (i) exempt?

options.D: The Rs. 1,65,000 performance fee is fully taxable since it EXCEEDS the Rs. 1,50,000 threshold under Entry 78 (the entire consideration, not merely the excess, becomes taxable); separately, the Rs. 480 per person admission fee at the cultural festival (event i) is exempt under Entry 81, since it does not exceed the Rs. 500 per person ceiling
options.A: Only the excess amount over Rs. 1,50,000 (i.e. Rs. 15,000) is taxable for the wedding performance, and the admission fee is taxable since Entry 81 applies only to circus and theatrical performances, not cultural festivals
options.B: The entire Rs. 1,65,000 performance fee is exempt since it is a classical dance performance regardless of amount, but the admission fee is taxable since it exceeds a Rs. 250 per person threshold under Entry 81
options.C: Both the performance fee and the admission fee are fully taxable, since Entry 78 and Entry 81 apply only to Government-organised cultural events, and this wedding/festival combination falls outside their scope

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. The Rs. 1,65,000 performance fee is fully taxable since it EXCEEDS the Rs. 1,50,000 threshold under Entry 78 (the entire consideration, not merely the excess, becomes taxable); separately, the Rs. 480 per person admission fee at the cultural festival (event i) is exempt under Entry 81, since it does not exceed the Rs. 500 per person ceiling

As per Entry 78, since the wedding reception performance fee (Rs. 1,65,000) EXCEEDS Rs. 1,50,000, the ENTIRE consideration becomes taxable (not merely the excess amount). Separately, as per Entry 81 of the Exemption Notification, right to admission to (among other things) a musical/dance performance or similar event is exempt where the consideration for admission does not exceed Rs. 500 per person; since the festival organiser at event (i) charges Rs. 480 per person (below this ceiling), the admission fee is exempt from GST.
